title: Terminalia chebula Extract Alleviates Lipopolysaccharide-Induced Acute Lung Injury by Modulating the Interleukin-17-Dependent Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase/Nuclear Factor-Kappa B Signaling Pathways.
authors: Li, Huifang; Bao, Shuguang; Bai, Laxinamujila; Li, Zhiqiang; Wang, Qinqin; Narenhu, Narenhu; Xiao, Xiaohe; Bao, Long; Bai, Tiankai
one_liner_zh: 该文研究植物提取物对急性肺损伤的抗炎作用，涉及分子对接与动力学模拟但对象为小分子-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI), a severe inflammatory disease, is intricately associated with the dysregulation of interleukin (IL)-17-mediated inflammatory responses. Terminalia chebula Retz., a traditional medicinal plant, can modulate inflammatory responses. We evaluated the effect of the prophylactic treatment using T. chebula extract (TCE) on lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced ALI and its underlying IL-17-linked mechanism. A mouse ALI model was established to assess TCE efficacy by observing histopathological and inflammatory changes. LC-MS identified its in vitro and absorbed components, followed by target prediction using integrated network pharmacology, molecular docking, and dynamics simulations, with key findings validated by Western blot analysis. ALI mice, pretreated with TCE, demonstrated notable improvements: lung tissue damage was alleviated and levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, tumor necrosis factor [TNF]-alpha, IL-17A) were reduced. Immunohistochemistry revealed that TCE markedly suppressed the enhanced alveolar expression of IL-17. Phytochemical analysis identified 55 constituents in TCE, with 15 bioactive compounds (e.g., ellagic acid, chebulinic acid) entering systemic circulation. Multi-method computational analysis confirmed that key compounds, particularly ellagic acid, stably interacted with core targets (e.g., IL-6, CXCL8). The KEGG analysis further highlighted significant enrichment in the IL-17 and NF-kappaB signaling pathways. These physiological adjustments coincided with the inhibition of the IL-17-MAPK/NF-kappaB pathway, as evidenced by decreased phosphorylation of p65, p38, and IkappaBalpha and downregulation of TLR4, MyD88, iNOS, and COX-2. Altogether, TCE pretreatment effectively alleviates ALI. The modulation of the IL-17-dependent signaling axis may enhance the resolution of inflammation, thereby reducing lung injury. These findings highlight the potential of TCE as a promising therapeutic for ALI via targeting the IL-17-MAPK/NF-kappaB pathway.
abstract_zh: 急性肺损伤（ALI）是一种严重的炎症性疾病，与白细胞介素（IL）-17介导的炎症反应失调密切相关。传统药用植物Terminalia chebula Retz.能够调节炎症反应。我们评估了使用T. chebula提取物（TCE）进行预防性治疗对脂多糖（LPS）诱导的ALI的效果及其潜在的IL-17相关机制。建立小鼠ALI模型，通过观察组织病理学和炎症变化来评估TCE的疗效。LC-MS鉴定了其体外及吸收成分，随后利用整合网络药理学、分子对接和动力学模拟进行靶点预测，并通过Western blot分析验证关键发现。经TCE预处理的ALI小鼠表现出显著改善：肺组织损伤减轻，促炎细胞因子（IL-6、肿瘤坏死因子[TNF]-α、IL-17A）水平降低。免疫组织化学显示，TCE显著抑制了肺泡中IL-17表达的增强。植物化学分析鉴定出TCE中的55种成分，其中15种生物活性化合物（如鞣花酸、诃子酸）进入体循环。多方法计算分析证实，关键化合物，尤其是鞣花酸，与核心靶点（如IL-6、CXCL8）稳定相互作用。KEGG分析进一步强调了IL-17和NF-kappaB信号通路的显著富集。这些生理调节与IL-17-MAPK/NF-kappaB通路的抑制相一致，表现为p65、p38和IkappaBalpha磷酸化降低以及TLR4、MyD88、iNOS和COX-2下调。总之，TCE预处理有效缓解ALI。对IL-17依赖性信号轴的调节可能增强炎症消退，从而减轻肺损伤。这些发现凸显了TCE通过靶向IL-17-MAPK/NF-kappaB通路作为ALI潜在治疗药物的前景。
